title: Good Controls Gone Bad: Difference-in-Differences with Covariates
abstract: arXiv:2412.14447v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper introduces the common causality of covariates (CCC) assumption in difference-in-differences with covariates. This assumption stipulates that covariates must have common effects on untreated potential outcomes across regions and periods. We also introduce Integrated Parallel Trends, a weaker alternative to conditional parallel trends that does not require point-wise equality of trends across covariate values, and can accommodate CCC violations. Pre-trend diagnostics for integrated parallel trends may reveal plausibly parallel trends that are obscured under conventional conditional parallel trends diagnostics, thereby broadening the set of empirical settings in which credible DID identification may be possible. Furthermore, we propose a new estimator called the Integrated Difference-in-Differences (DID-INT) estimator, which can identify the ATT when integrated parallel trends holds and the CCC assumption is violated. translated_title: “好的控制变量”何以变坏：含协变量的双重差分法
translated_abstract: 本文在含协变量的双重差分法（DID）中引入了协变量共同因果性假设。该假设规定，协变量必须在所有地区和时期上对未处理的潜在结果具有共同的影响。我们还提出了“整合平行趋势”，这是条件平行趋势的一种更弱的替代方案，它不要求趋势在协变量的各个取值上逐点相等，并且能够容忍CCC假设的违反。针对整合平行趋势的事前趋势诊断可能会揭示出在传统条件平行趋势诊断下被掩盖的合理平行趋势，从而扩大了可能实现可信DID识别的实证研究场景的范围。此外，我们提出了一种新的估计量，称为整合双重差分估计量（DID-INT），当整合平行趋势成立且CCC假设被违反时，该估计量仍能识别平均处理效应（ATT）。
tldr: 本文提出协变量共同因果性假设与更弱的“整合平行趋势”条件，并据此设计了DID-INT估计量，使得在传统条件平行趋势无法成立或诊断失效的情境下仍能可靠地识别处理效应。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the common causality of covariates (CCC) assumption and a weaker Integrated Parallel Trends condition, and proposes the DID-INT estimator, which can identify the ATT even when conventional conditional parallel trends fails and the CCC assumption is violated.
